newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya to hold local polls in January - agency.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya to hold local polls in January - agency.

text.p: The separatist Chechen leadership, retaking effective control of the breakaway province as Russian troops withdraw under a peace deal, plans to hold local elections next January, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.
Interfax also said the separatists, evidently without Moscow's approval, had finalised the line up of a "coalition government" in Chechnya, but it gave no details.

Interfax said the poll decision had been taken at a meeting of top rebel commanders late on Monday. It did not make clear whether the polls would simply elect local councils in Chechen towns and villages or would choose a national leader as well.

Moscow and the rebels struck a peace deal for the region on August 31 under which Russia agreed to withdraw its forces in exchange for postponing any decision of the region's future political status for five years.
Moscow still rules out independence for Chechnya, but rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev has said repeatedly he will not give up the separatist struggle.

A pro-Moscow government which had run the province since the start of conflict has been sidelined by the peace deal and its leader Doku Zavgayev is not involved in the latest rounds of negotiations between Moscow and the separatists.

Moscow has not officially protested against the separatists' decision to name a coalition government. It was not clear whether Russia, evidently uninvolved in fixing a date for local elections, would recognise their results.
President Boris Yeltsin, who is preparing for heart surgery, on Monday named his security supremo Alexander Lebed as Moscow's chief negotiator in Chechnya.
Interfax quoted Lebed's aide Sergei Kharlamov, who is due in Chechnya on Wednesday, as saying he would discuss local elections with the rebels.
Interfax said the rebel leaders also approved a 30-member delegation for further talks with Russia.
